blocks.text:
Warning: serious infections, malignancy and thrombosis
Serious infections, including tuberculosis, some fatal, malignancies including lymphoma, and venous thromboembolism have been reported (see 【不良反应】 and 【注意事项】). Screen for tuberculosis before treatment.
Common name: Lumiravostat Tablets
Trade name: Ostrevia
English name: Lumiravostat Tablets
Pinyin: Lumiruowasita Pian
The active ingredient is lumiravostat.
Excipients: microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow).
10 mg: white, round, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "10" on the other.
25 mg: yellow, oval, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "25" on the other.
For adults with moderate to severe chronic hand eczema that has not responded adequately to potent topical corticosteroids, or when these are not advisable.
The recommended dose is 10 mg once daily, with or without food. The dose may be increased to 25 mg once daily if the response is inadequate after 12 weeks.
Moderate hepatic impairment: 10 mg once daily. Severe hepatic impairment: not recommended.
With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (for example ketoconazole or clarithromycin): 10 mg once daily.

blocks.text: Serious infections, including tuberculosis, pneumonia, cellulitis and herpes zoster, have been reported, some leading to hospitalization or death. Screen patients for latent tuberculosis before starting treatment and treat it first. Interrupt treatment if a serious infection develops.
Malignancy, including lymphoma and non-melanoma skin cancer, has been reported. Consider the risks and benefits before starting treatment in patients with a known malignancy.
Venous thromboembolism, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, has been reported. Use with caution in patients with risk factors and stop treatment if it occurs.
Monitor lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin and liver enzymes at baseline, at 4 weeks and every 3 months.

Lumiravostat caused embryo-fetal toxicity in rats and rabbits. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose.
It is not known whether lumiravostat passes into human milk. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose.
The safety and efficacy in children under 18 years have not been established; no clinical study was done in children and there is no reliable reference.
Infections occurred more often in patients aged 65 and over. Use with care while monitoring the patient.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase lumiravostat exposure (use 10 mg once daily). Strong CYP3A4 inducers, such as rifampicin, reduce exposure; avoid concomitant use.
There is no specific antidote. Monitor the patient for signs of adverse reactions and give supportive treatment. Lumiravostat is not removed by haemodialysis to a meaningful extent.
Lumiravostat is a reversible inhibitor of the fictional STRK1 kinase, which signals downstream of several cytokines involved in skin inflammation.
Dose-dependent reductions in markers of skin inflammation were seen within 2 weeks.
Peak plasma concentrations are reached 1 to 2 hours after a dose. The half-life is about 16 hours. Lumiravostat is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4.

In two 16-week placebo-controlled studies (fictional HANDS-1 and HANDS-2, 1,210 adults), 38% of patients on lumiravostat 25 mg and 31% on 10 mg reached clear or almost clear hands, against 12% on placebo.
Lumiravostat was not genotoxic. Embryo-fetal toxicity was seen in rats and rabbits at exposures close to the human exposure at 25 mg.
Store below 30°C, in the original package to protect from moisture.
Aluminium/aluminium blister, 14 tablets per blister, 2 blisters per box.
